categories.summary: All Australian carriers normal and the global threat level is green. France has blamed Iran's IRGC for hacking supermarket freezer systems in Europe. A Westpac online-banking outage was reported on 10 Nov; no sign it was an attack. Overnight cable-vessel alerts were not confirmed. ACSC feed timed out.

categories.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has passed 10,600 cases with spread to Kenya and Nigeria; no cases outside Africa. Pandemic-response stocks are up (Moderna +12% over 5 days), which is worth watching but has no matching outbreak news. Adelaide EDs: one very busy (Flinders).

categories.summary: Fire danger Moderate in the Mount Lofty Ranges, no rating for Adelaide, no fire bans and no CFS warnings. Several outback roads in the north-east remain closed by flooding. No GDACS orange/red alerts or M6+ quakes.

headline: Watch: the Iran-Hormuz standoff keeps fuel the main risk for SA; overnight cable-vessel alerts were not confirmed and all networks are normal.
summary: Little change overnight. US-Iran strikes and talks over Hormuz continue side by side, and Houthi forces have attacked Riyadh again, but Brent oil eased to about US$91.80. The vessels flagged near Australian cable corridors overnight have moved on, with no damage or network outage. In SA, fire danger is Moderate in the Mount Lofty Ranges and a few outback roads remain closed by flooding.
